summary: Search a field for a value using the active FileMaker transport.
purpose: Use this when you want a plain-English search example that stays read-only.
learningGoals: See how Data API finds use a query array while OData finds use a filter expression.
Practice carrying a field name and value through both transports honestly.
Learn a safe browser request shape for transport-specific searches.
explanation: Find is the first place the two FileMaker transports become meaningfully different. This module keeps both variants explicit so beginners do not assume the same payload works everywhere.
commonMistakes: Typing the field label instead of the real FileMaker field name.
Expecting a Data API query array to work in OData.
Forgetting that OData string values need quote escaping.
expectedResult: You get starter code that searches one field in a transport-correct way without changing data.

prerequisites: Know the exact FileMaker field name you want to search.
Keep search requests routed through the authenticated PHP bridge.

inputs.label: Layout or table
inputs.help: Use the layout name for Data API or the table name for OData.

inputs.label: Field name
inputs.help: Use the exact FileMaker field name, including capitalization and spacing if your schema uses them.

inputs.label: Value to match
inputs.help: Use the value you want the field to match.

inputs.label: How many matches
inputs.help: Keep the first search small so your test stays fast and readable.

beginner: Find is still safe because it only reads matching records.
Data API searches use a query array, but OData searches use a filter expression.
Keep the real FileMaker field name exactly as your schema defines it.
advanced: The OData PHP variant uses separate placeholder escaping for the field token and the quoted value.
The JavaScript OData variant serializes the value with OData-safe quote doubling before sending it to PHP.
This module preserves the old PHP generator output exactly while making the transport split explicit.
